_about: Direct far JMPs from a movable code segment to a movable segment of the same module. nevalid.py rejects every such jump unless it is listed here with matching target and context bytes. Each entry says why the far return on the stack at that jump is not a CS:IP pushed by hand in the jumping segment. A jump that a push walk proves is reached from a "push cs / push" pair is rejected even if listed. Entries marked provisional have not been fully established and need an independent check; a RESIDUAL note names what was observed rather than proven.

farjmp.why: tail jump out of the program entry (exported ordinal 100, 1:0000). No PUSH CS between the entry and this jump; the far return on the stack is the one pushed by the application stub's far CALL to ordinal 100.

jump into the runtime error raiser (entries 7:0279..0292 fall through to the raiser body at 7:0294; error number in BL/BX). The far return on the stack at this jump is never consumed by a RETF: the raiser body 7:0294..030B branches only within itself and leaves only through 'call 0204 / ret' at 7:0308; 7:0204 is 'mov ax,[2518] / call far 4:173A'; 4:173A..17ED has only forward branches and ends in 'call far 2:0FCA' (4:17F2 is a separate procedure entry); 2:0FCA begins 'pop bx / pop bx', discarding its own return address, restores the interpreter state from the frame at SP and leaves by a near RET in segment 2. So 4:173A, 7:0204 and the raiser never return, and 7:030B is never executed after the call. SP was set at 4:17AA ('mov sp,ax', AX from 2:42E7: the active VB error context's frame) or, when [008A] is set, at 7:0093 ('mov sp,[008A]'). The slot at this jump is used again only if that reset lands at or below it, i.e. inside the raising code's own frames, which would make 2:0FCA restore the raiser's frames as the error context and break the runtime the same way in protected mode. RESIDUAL (observed, not proven): that the reset target always encloses the raising code.
exported entry thunk (ordinal 691 = 7:05DC is this JMP itself): the far return on the stack is the far caller's.

Accepted (review R15-2) for this converted DLL: 7:008E (ordinal 110, a converter-created export; the original had a near call) is reached only by two relocations, both wrapper stubs in FIXED segment 24: 24:0B42 (caller segment 2, used by 2:496B) and 24:0BB7 (caller segment 7, used by 7:1966, the trampoline for "push cs / call" at 7:00C9). No near call, jump, branch or 0x008E immediate in segment 7 reaches it, and the table at 7:0000 is read only by "jmp cs:[bx-2]" at 7:008E. So the far return on the stack at this jump is always a wrapper return in a fixed segment. LIMITATION: a module other than this one importing ordinal 110 is not covered.
